title: Materialized View

validation.research: Ten primary documentation references: Microsoft defines the broad architectural projection; PostgreSQL documents persisted query results and non-incremental concurrent refresh requirements; ClickHouse documents inserted-block/partial-state/right-side-join behavior and full-refresh replacement; BigQuery documents query rewriting, combining stored/new data, eligibility/fallback and staleness; SQLite documents connection isolation, serialized writers and trigger abort; Python sqlite3 documents explicit transactions, rollback and separate connection cleanup. Materialized View is the established singular title, former Materialized Views an alias. Architectural maintenance is distinguished from native database objects, ordinary views, query-result caching and CQRS. Existing useful sales100->110, correction/deletion, grain/currency, additive state, backfill, lag/completeness and three-engine contexts are retained. The runnable application-maintained SQLite example is not claimed to implement native PostgreSQL/ClickHouse/BigQuery behavior.

example_limits: Revised existing canonical data-materialized-views in place. Singular Materialized View becomes title; plural former title is an alias. Existing summary, Data Engineering tags/verse, canonical ID/route and primary figure path preserved. One primary home moves from Storage & access to Performance and Scalability; former collection retains a cross-link and fifteen other members. Original historical import metadata remains untouched; old article and figure archived locally. Retains sales100->110, currency/grain, correction50->40, backfill boundary, aggregate-state, PostgreSQL/ClickHouse/BigQuery and refresh/completeness teaching context. Original Python 3.11+ application-maintained SQLite projection, not a native SQLite materialized-view object. Positive/zero integer cents grouped by shop/currency; three USD sales5000+3000+2000 create generation1/count3/10000. Appended1000 leaves staleG1 until refreshG2/count4/11000. Correction5000->4000 and deletion3000 make source3/7000. An AFTER UPDATE publication trigger raises ABORT after candidate update; connection context rolls back deleted/rebuilt rows and generation toG2/count4/11000. Removing trigger and retrying publishesG3/count3/7000 without additive replay. Generation is a publication identity, not time/source watermark; zero generation is unavailable and an empty refreshed group is valid zero. BEGIN IMMEDIATE with idle explicit-transaction connection serializes SQLite writers; target and metadata change in one transaction; connection owner closes it. Actual separate-connection WAL tests verify old reads during refresh, reader snapshot lifetime and writer exclusion. No production database-native refresh implementation, incremental updater, scheduler, change stream, authorization, source watermark, cross-store snapshot or freshness deadline is supplied.
